title: Gel-seq: A Method for Simultaneous Sequencing Library Preparation of DNA and RNA Using Hydrogel Matrices
protocol: Sterilize 50 mL of purified, deionized water in a UV crosslinking oven for 15 min (15 mJ/cm² total exposure).
Heat sterilized water to 37°C for use in following steps.
Weigh 3.867 g of acrylamide monomer and 0.133 g of bis-acrylamide monomer.
Combine the weighed acrylamide and bis-acrylamide with warm purified water up to a total volume of 10 mL.
Vortex until dissolved and store protected from light at room temperature.
Weigh 4.750 g of acrylamide monomer and 0.250 g of bis-acrylamide monomer.
Combine the weighed acrylamide and bis-acrylamide with warm purified water up to a total volume of 10 mL.
Vortex until dissolved and store protected from light at room temperature.
Add 5 g sucrose to a graduated cylinder.
Add warm purified water up to a total volume of 10 mL.
Vortex until dissolved and store at room temperature.
Add 1 g of ammonium persulfate (APS) to a graduated cylinder.
Add cold (~4°C) purified water up to a total volume of 10 mL.
Vortex until dissolved.
Freeze in aliquots of 200 μL.
Prepare gel precursors in three separate plastic tubes by adding the specified reagents for each type of gel (Filler, High Density, and Low Density).
Vortex ingredients to mix thoroughly without adding APS or TEMED yet.
Add 104.0 µL of ammonium persulfate (10% w/v) to the Filler Gel Precursor tube.
Add 6.0 µL of TEMED to the Filler Gel Precursor tube and immediately pour into the cassette.
Add 50.0 µL of ammonium persulfate (10% w/v) to the High Density Gel Precursor tube.
Add 1.0 µL of TEMED to the High Density Gel Precursor tube and immediately pour into the cassette.
Add 39.0 µL of ammonium persulfate (10% w/v) to the Low Density Gel Precursor tube.
Add 2.2 µL of TEMED to the Low Density Gel Precursor tube and immediately pour into the cassette.
De-gas gel monomer solutions by inserting a needle through the cap and connecting it to a house vacuum line.
Submerge the assembly in an ultrasonic bath set to high until bubbles stop emerging (~60 seconds per tube).
Add TEMED and APS to the filler gel precursor and vortex briefly.
Pipette 6 mL of the filler gel precursor into each gel cassette using six increments of 1 mL each.
Ensure the fluid is level by positioning the cassettes upright on a level table.
Fill the remainder of the cassette with deionized, degassed water using six increments of 1 mL each.
Allow the polymer to cure for at least one hour, up to overnight.
Invert the gel cassettes over a sink to remove the water overlay.
Use a compressed air gun to gently dry the interface by blowing air through the top opening from a distance of 6 inches.
Add TEMED and APS to the high-density gel precursor.
Vortex briefly.
Pipette 320 µL of the high-density precursor into the cassette using a 1 mL pipette.
Rock the cassette back and forth around 3 times to ensure even coating.
Fill the remainder of the cassette with deionized, degassed water using a 1 mL pipette slowly.
Allow the polymer to cure for at least fifteen minutes.
Invert the gel cassettes to remove the water overlay.
Use compressed air to gently dry the interface.
Add TEMED and APS to the low-density gel precursor.
Vortex briefly.
Fill the remainder of the cassette (~1.65 mL) with the low-density gel precursor using a pipette.
Insert the gel comb.
Pipette an excess of reserve precursor at the top of the comb.
Allow the polymer to cure for at least 4 hours.
Store gels in TBE buffer for up to a week or more.
Use a hemocytometer or an automatic cell counter to calculate the cell concentration in a suspension of cells of interest.
Dilute the cells to a concentration of 100 to 1000 cells per μL in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Mix 19 µL of lysis buffer and 1 µL of RNase inhibitor to prepare a 10X stock solution of reaction buffer.
Create a lysis master mix containing 0.5 µL of reaction buffer and 2.75 µL of nuclease-free water for each sample.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down 5 times to re-suspend settled cells.
Pipette 1 µL of cell suspension into a 200 µL nuclease-free strip tube sterilized by UV.
Repeat pipetting steps as necessary depending on number of samples, including a negative control with 1 µL of nuclease-free water instead of cells for one reaction.
Add 3.25 µL of lysis master mix to each sample and mix by gently pipetting up and down 5 times.
Preheat a thermal cycler (with heated lid) to 72 °C.
Add 1 µL of RT primer and 1 µL of 20 µM random hexamer with WTA adapter (5′-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTAC-NNNNNN-3′) to each sample.
Reserve at least one tube as a positive control for gDNA library preparation and add 2 µL of water instead of primers.
Incubate samples at 72 °C in the preheated thermal cycler for 3 minutes to lyse the cells.
Remove cells from thermal cycler and place on ice for 2 minutes.
Store the positive control at 4 °C until step 5.

While the cells are lysing, create a sufficient volume of reverse transcription master mix containing: 2 µL of first strand buffer, 0.5 µL of template switch oligonucleotide (TSO), 0.25 µL of RNase inhibitor, and 1 µL of reverse transcriptase (100 U/µL).
Preheat thermal cycler to 42 °C.
Add 3.75 µL of reverse transcription master mix to the remaining samples, bringing the total sample volume to 10 µL.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Perform reverse transcription by immediately placing samples in a preheated thermal cycler.
Run the following program: 42 °C for 90 min, 70 °C for 10 min, 4 °C forever.
Carefully clean a gel electrophoresis chamber using a DNA removal product.
Apply several mL of liquid cleaning agent to a disposable lint free wipe and wipe across all surfaces of the chamber.
Fill the chamber with clean 0.5x TBE.
Place the entire apparatus in a 254 nm UV crosslinking oven.
Sterilize for 15 minutes (15 mJ/cm²).
Insert the Gel-seq cassette into the gel electrophoresis chamber and lock it into place.
Slowly remove the gel comb by pulling straight up.
Keep samples from step 3 on ice, reserving one as a positive control for cDNA library generation.
Store the reserved sample at 4 °C until step 6.
Add 2 µL of 6X loading dye to the remaining samples, bringing the total volume to ~12 µL.
Thoroughly mix the samples by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Combine 1 µL of a DNA ladder with 2 µL of 6x loading dye and 7 µL of water.
Pipette this mixture into lane 1 of the Gel-seq cassette as an electrophoresis control.
Pipette the samples from the previous step into separate lanes of the Gel-seq cassette.
Apply an electric field of 250 V across the Gel-seq cassette for 30 minutes to separate gDNA from cDNA/RNA hybrids.
Remove the Gel-seq cassette from the gel electrophoresis chamber.
Open the two halves of the cassette by prying the edges with a scraping tool.
Using a scalpel, cut the gel in half just below the high-density layer.
Discard the half containing filler gel by picking it up with gloved hands.
Gently peel the remaining gel off of the cassette using a paint scraper or similar tool.
Place this section of the gel into a dish containing ~30 mL of 0.5x TBE and 3 µL of gel stain.
Cover the container to minimize photobleaching and soak the gel while gently shaking for 5 minutes.
Place the gel on plastic wrap and take a UV image using a gel documentation system.
Verify that separation has occurred by confirming results from the gel documentation system.
Move the gel to a UV transilluminator, wearing appropriate UV glasses.
Cut out regions of the gel containing gDNA and cDNA.
Cut a 4 mm by 10 mm rectangular section of gel for sample recovery; adjust geometry based on electrophoresis system used.
Remember to cut the lane loaded with the negative control.
Place each excised section of gel into a strip tube using blunt-end tweezers.
Grind the gel in each tube with the tip of a pipette by moving it in a circular motion against the bottom of the tube.
Add 40 μL of nuclease-free water to gDNA samples and 80 μL to cDNA samples before removing the pipette tip to minimize sample loss.
Place the strip tubes into a vortex mixer inside a 37 °C incubator and shake for 8 - 12 hours.
Pipette the samples into an 8 µm mesh filter plate and spin at 2600 x g for 5 minutes to strain out gel fragments.
Lift the mesh filter plate away from the housing plate and pipette the gel-free water samples into a new 200 μL strip tube.
Add 1 μL of protease (0.9 AU/mL) to each sample containing gDNA, mix well by pipetting up and down.
Incubate at 50 °C for 15 minutes followed by heat inactivation at 70 °C for 15 minutes.
Using an 18 gauge needle, poke holes in the caps of all sample tubes.
Place the samples in a vacufuge to reduce liquid volume.
Reduce gDNA samples to 5 µL and cDNA samples to 10 µL.
Quantify DNA concentration in each gDNA sample using a fluorometer or similar technology.
Dilute gDNA samples to 0.2 ng/µL of DNA.
Add 12.5 µL of 2X qPCR mix, 0.5 µL cDNA PCR primer, and 2 µL nuclease-free water to the cDNA samples.
Complete gDNA library preparation by following the half reaction volume protocol.
Perform PCR in a real-time thermocycler.
Set the hot-start temperature to 95 °C for 3 min.
Cycle through 20-30 cycles of 98 °C for 10 s, 65 °C for 30 s, and 72 °C for 3 min.
Monitor reaction curves during amplification.
Stop the amplification before reactions leave the exponential phase to avoid overamplification.
Clean the PCR product using SPRI beads following step 8 protocol.
Quantify DNA concentration in each cDNA sample and positive control from step 4 using a fluorometer or similar technology.
Dilute samples if necessary to contain approximately 0.2 ng/µL of DNA.
Optional: Perform polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis on 1 - 2 µL of each qPCR product to validate library generation reaction.
Complete cDNA library preparation by following the half volume reaction protocol.
UV sterilize strip tubes for the number of samples to be processed.
Add 5 μL transposase buffer to each strip tube.
Add 2.5 μL input DNA at 0.2 ng/μL to each sample.
Add 2.5 μL transposase to each sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Incubate the samples at 55 °C for 5 minutes.
Hold the samples at 10 °C.
After reaching 10 °C, add 2.5 μL transposase stop buffer to each sample.
Keep the samples at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Mix 7.5 µL of library prep PCR mix with the sample.
Add 2.5 µL of an index 1 primer to the mixture.
Add 2.5 µL of an index 2 primer to the mixture.
Pipette up and down 5 times to mix well.
Incubate at 72 °C for 3 minutes.
Incubate at 95 °C for 30 seconds.
Perform 12 cycles:
Incubate at 95 °C for 10 seconds.
Incubate at 72 °C for 30 seconds.
Incubate at 55 °C for 30 seconds.
Incubate at 72 °C for 5 minutes.
Hold at 10 °C.
Prepare SPRI beads in 1.5 mL aliquots and bring to room temperature before use.
Prepare fresh 80% ethanol for each experiment.
Clean the prepared libraries using SPRI beads following the protocol.
Validate the cleaned libraries using gel electrophoresis or a similar assay.
Add 1 µl of WTA kit lysis buffer to each PCR product.
Vortex SPRI beads until evenly mixed.
Add 50 µl of SPRI beads to each sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Incubate samples at room temperature for 8 minutes.
Briefly spin the samples to collect liquid from tube sides.
Place samples on a magnetic separation device for ~5 minutes until clear.
Pipette off and discard supernatant without disturbing beads.
Add 200 µL of 80% ethanol to each sample without disturbing beads.
Wait for 30 seconds, then pipette off supernatant.
Repeat ethanol wash once.
Allow samples to dry for 30 s - 1 min.
Remove samples from magnetic separation device.
Add 15 µL of water to each sample to elute DNA.
Pipette up and down to ensure beads are removed.
Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Briefly spin the samples.
Place samples on a magnetic separation device for ~1 minute until clear.
While the samples are on the magnetic separation device, slowly pipette up the supernatant and transfer it to clean tubes.
Be careful not to disturb the ring of beads on the tube.
Discard the tubes with beads.
